sections.title: CUA-Universe: A Scalable and Dynamic Environment for Hybrid GUI+CLI Agents
sections.abstract: A pipeline turns real desktop software into scalable hybrid GUI+CLI environments, generates controllable tasks, and harvests efficient trajectories for computer-use-agent training.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors report gains on CUA-Verse, OSWorld, and OSWorld-MCP, including a 39.3-point CUA-Verse score improvement and 60% fewer tokens.
sections.caveat: The environment covers 16 applications; broader real-world coverage and robustness remain open.

sections.title: Multi-Step Tool-Calling over Korean Open Public APIs: A Benchmark and a Data-Synthesis Recipe
sections.abstract: KOPA-Bench contains 145 multi-step tasks over live Korean public APIs, while EDGE uses successful live tool executions to synthesize executable trajectories for GRPO fine-tuning.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors report that a GRPO-trained 9B model nearly matches an untuned 27B model and improves on KOPA-Bench and BFCL.
sections.caveat: Transfer beyond the country- and domain-specific API ecosystem is not established by the abstract.

sections.title: RISE: Recursive Improvement via Self-Extrapolating Policy Distillation
sections.abstract: RISE constructs a synthetic teacher from a model’s own RLVR trajectory by extrapolating checkpoint or logit changes, combining outcome rewards with dense token-level self-distillation.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors report improvements over RLVR-only training and on-policy self-distillation across math, STEM, code, and multi-turn agentic tasks.
sections.caveat: The abstract does not provide enough detail to assess variance or statistical significance of the gains.

sections.title: Don't Drop Dropout: Optimizing Layer Sparsity for Efficient LLM Training and Inference
sections.abstract: Across more than 2,400 experiments, the paper studies layer dropout as a training and post-training efficiency technique for LLMs.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors report up to 25% training-FLOP savings and up to 1.5x inference speedup with negligible accuracy loss under tuned settings.
sections.caveat: Results were run on Cerebras CS-3 systems and may depend on hardware, model family, and optimizer choices.

sections.title: TruthInsightBench: An Evidence-Grounded Benchmark for Automated Evaluation of Open-Ended Scientific Discovery Agents
sections.abstract: TruthInsightBench evaluates scientific-discovery agents on 40 blind tasks from 10 domains, scoring evidence quality rather than reproduction of known analyses.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors report a narrow 58.4–60.3/100 plateau for four coding agents and identify scientific judgment as the main bottleneck.
sections.caveat: The benchmark uses a fixed LLM-based judge and 40 tasks, so judge validity and scientific coverage require further study.
